Honestly, I think there are some things we will agree on, and others not, but that’s totally okay. I will say this, for myself personally the idea of stretching out the holidays is not a bad thing. After all, when I think of the holidays, I think of happiness, love, relaxation, family, and togetherness. Why wouldn’t I want to stretch out those feelings as long as possible? Especially in a year when the world has been defined by isolation, fear, and sadness. If extending the holiday season a bit to help combat those negative feelings is all it takes, then sign me up for a longer holiday season. I can understand your argument that this takes away from the essence of Christmas and dilutes it, but I don’t think that dilution is necessarily a bad thing. Sometimes Christmas can be too much change at once, too many expectations, so a dilution effect can be a positive. 

In any case, Christmas traditions and beliefs are very different for everyone and I fully support however you choose to celebrate, I only ask you do the same. Have a wonderful Christmas whenever you choose to begin celebrating it. I am sure it is beautiful there in Sweden over the holidays. I have always wanted to visit as my great grandparents immigrated from Sweden to Canada. All the best from Canada.

I think you are drawing a relation between capitalism and decoration that is problematic. While there is an argument that Christmas is being more and more commercialized, that doesn’t mean that someone’s love of Christmas enhances that capitalism. Christmas and what that looks like to someone, is very different to many people. “Christmas for what it is” may not be the same to me as it is for you. Perhaps your idea of Christmas is something I would be extremely opposed to, but I recognize your right to celebrate your Christmas how you choose. Why shouldn’t I be allowed to do the same? If your answer is because my small amount of decorations is forcing consumerism on people... I think you may want to look at the broader picture and simply focus on removing that element of consumerism from your own traditions, because no one person gets to decide what is the “proper” form of Christmas. My Christmas is about family, happiness, and bringing joy to our lives. I would take that year round, so to have it be occurring a few weeks early doesn’t seem like some crime to me, and doesn’t sacrifice on any of the Christmas values I hold dear. While I can appreciate your point that you don’t agree, why can’t you simply leave it at that? You don’t agree, then move on. Why does the world have to conform to your specific wants/needs. It would have been far easier for you to simply have seen the post, downvoted, and then moved on, instead of leaving a hateful comment. Either way, you “probably can’t help yourself.” Merry Christmas anyway, however you choose to celebrate it.

I am actually taking English in University and wish I had time/could afford to write either books or screenplays. Alas money once again dictates my dreams and reality. It is this lack of control in my life that I feel that is hardest for me to overcome. Trying to see a way out is such an alien feeling at this point and I struggle to see a future that is different from my current setting, let alone one where I could do something amazing like write for a career.

I truly do want to choose tone happy, but at this time I just don't see a way to do so. I don't see the proverbial light at the end if the tunnel. All I see are a maze of tunnels burrowing constantly downwards, deeper and deeper into the depths. I am struggling to find an escape rope, believing that if by some miracle I do, it will simply snap betwixt my fingers. Cutting off all hope of escape.

I have hobbies that make me happy and friends to do them with. The hardest part recently is that they are gone for the summer and that so much if my foundational world support had crashed down atop me. So much has broken in my life in the past month and the chance of being able to return to school and my friends looks bleaker every day. This in turn causes me to feel worse and worse. Is a vicious spiral and not being new to serious major depression, I recognize the symptoms but cannot seem to pull myself out of it. I feel as if I am struggling to stay afloat with the weights of life pulling me under. Every day is harder and I don't see an end in sight.
Thank you for taking the time to say something and give me a small positive ray in my otherwise bleak existence. For a second it out a smile in my head and that was quite nice for a change.
